questions.stem: What topology does the supplied CLZ-170 configuration create?

options.A: Four VNets connected by peering.
options.B: One VNet and four distinct subnets.
options.C: One VM in each subnet.
options.D: A public load balancer and Bastion.

optionExplanations.A: Only one VNet is declared.
optionExplanations.B: The subnets represent web, app, data, and management roles.
optionExplanations.C: No workloads are deployed.
optionExplanations.D: Neither service is declared.

questions.stem: Why must 10.40.1.0/24 fit inside the VNet's 10.40.0.0/16?

options.A: A /24 always requires a public IP.
options.B: The numbers encode Azure region eastus2.
options.C: A subnet prefix must be contained in the VNet address space.

optionExplanations.A: Private subnet ranges do not require public addresses.
optionExplanations.B: CIDRs are independent of region names.
optionExplanations.C: The subnet partitions that network's configured address range.
optionExplanations.D: Tags do not define subnet containment.

questions.stem: A new app subnet reuses the web subnet's exact prefix. What is the problem?

options.A: Their tags must have matching case.
options.B: Both need a public IP before creation.
options.C: The subscription requires a Windows image.

optionExplanations.A: Tag case is unrelated to address overlap.
optionExplanations.B: Subnets can exist without public IPs.
optionExplanations.C: There is no workload image requirement here.
optionExplanations.D: The address plan must keep them distinct.

questions.stem: Do the names web, app, data, and mgmt alone enforce firewall policy between those tiers?

options.A: No; names and subnet separation are not an NSG policy.
options.B: Yes; data automatically denies all inbound packets.
options.C: Yes; mgmt automatically enables Bastion.

optionExplanations.A: This lesson deliberately adds no NSGs.
optionExplanations.B: A name does not create rules.
optionExplanations.C: Bastion is not declared.
optionExplanations.D: No port-opening rule is created.

questions.stem: Which validation query checks the deployed VNet's address prefixes?

options.A: terraform fmt -check only.
options.B: az network vnet show with addressSpace.addressPrefixes.
options.C: az account show --query tenantId.

optionExplanations.A: Formatting does not query Azure.
optionExplanations.B: It reads the VNet configuration from Azure.
optionExplanations.C: That reads directory context.
optionExplanations.D: No password output exists here.

questions.stem: Which prefix does the provided mgmt subnet use?

optionExplanations.A: That belongs to data-snet.
optionExplanations.B: That is the VNet's complete address space.
optionExplanations.C: It is explicitly declared for mgmt-snet.
optionExplanations.D: That is not the management subnet declaration.

questions.stem: Why can CLZ-170 be validated without checking VM power state?

options.A: All its VMs are hidden.
options.B: VNet creation automatically deallocates VMs.
options.C: Terraform cannot read VM properties.

optionExplanations.A: There are no VM resources.
optionExplanations.B: It does not create or deallocate hidden VMs.
optionExplanations.C: Later lessons can inspect them.
optionExplanations.D: Validation focuses on address-space and subnet properties.

questions.stem: Which proposed extra subnet is contained in the lesson's 10.40.0.0/16 VNet and does not overlap its four supplied /24 ranges?

optionExplanations.A: It remains inside the /16 and outside the existing four ranges.
optionExplanations.B: It overlaps the existing web /24.
optionExplanations.C: It is outside the VNet's configured /16.
optionExplanations.D: It repeats the management range.

questions.stem: A candidate peered VNet uses 10.40.0.0/16 too. What must be resolved first?

options.A: Only its Project tag.
options.B: Its overlapping address space.
options.C: Only whether the candidate uses the same region.

optionExplanations.A: Tags do not solve routing ambiguity.
optionExplanations.B: Peering requires nonoverlapping address spaces.
optionExplanations.C: Region choice does not repair overlapping address spaces.
optionExplanations.D: A title does not change network prefixes.

questions.stem: The learner changes location to an approved alternative region. Must the private CIDR change solely for that reason?

options.A: Yes; eastus2 owns the 10.40 range.
options.B: Yes; Terraform maps every region to one /16.
options.C: No; region and IP addressing are separate choices.
options.D: Only the management CIDR must become public.

optionExplanations.A: Private ranges are not assigned to regions that way.
optionExplanations.B: No such map is defined.
optionExplanations.C: The address plan is not encoded by the location string.
optionExplanations.D: That is not required.

questions.stem: Why allocate from an organization-wide IP plan for production?

options.A: To replace RBAC authentication.
options.B: To guarantee every VM is free.
options.C: To make subnet names immutable.
options.D: To avoid overlap across connected networks.

optionExplanations.A: IP planning does not grant permissions.
optionExplanations.B: Addresses do not waive billing.
optionExplanations.C: The purpose is coordinated addressing.
optionExplanations.D: Later hub, peering, and hybrid paths need compatible addressing.

questions.stem: CLZ-170's VNet is under a CLZ-170 group. Should the learner assume it modifies CLZ-160's group?

options.A: No; this lesson declares its own lifecycle boundary.
options.B: Yes; every lesson shares the same resource group.
options.C: Only when the Environment tag matches.
options.D: Yes; prerequisite order automatically imports resources.

optionExplanations.A: Its naming uses a different fixed lesson code.
optionExplanations.B: The source uses independent declarations and names.
optionExplanations.C: A shared tag does not merge ownership.
optionExplanations.D: Navigation does not perform import.

questions.stem: What should az network vnet subnet list show after the supplied deployment?

options.A: One subnet per Azure region.
options.B: Four subnet entries with distinct prefixes.
options.C: No subnets until a VM is attached.

optionExplanations.A: Subnets belong to the chosen VNet.
optionExplanations.B: Exactly four subnet resources are declared.
optionExplanations.C: Empty subnets can be deployed.
optionExplanations.D: Assessments do not create networks.

questions.stem: Does this configuration create a public IP for the web subnet?

options.A: Yes; web subnets always get one.
options.B: Only if the VNet prefix is /16.
options.C: No; no public IP resource is declared.
options.D: Yes; Azure bills one IP for every subnet.

optionExplanations.A: Public IPs are separately configured resources.
optionExplanations.B: CIDR size does not create public IPs.
optionExplanations.C: The word web is a role label only.
optionExplanations.D: That is not the declared architecture.

questions.stem: Each subnet references azurerm_virtual_network.main.name. What does that reference establish in Terraform?

options.A: An automatic NSG association.
options.B: A public DNS zone.
options.C: A dependency on every repository lesson.
options.D: A dependency on the VNet's configured result.

optionExplanations.A: That needs its own declaration.
optionExplanations.B: No DNS zone is declared.
optionExplanations.C: The reference is in this module.
optionExplanations.D: Terraform can order related resource actions from references.

questions.stem: Which production addition controls custom traffic paths rather than simply naming subnet tiers?

options.A: Route tables with deliberate routes.
options.B: An Environment tag.
options.C: A subnet name changed to default-route.

optionExplanations.A: Routes express next-hop decisions.
optionExplanations.B: Tags classify metadata.
optionExplanations.C: Renaming does not create route entries.
optionExplanations.D: Names are not routes.

questions.stem: Why are not all 256 addresses in an Azure IPv4 /24 subnet available for workloads?

options.A: A /24 contains only four addresses.
options.B: Azure reserves five addresses per subnet.
options.C: Every address is reserved for Terraform.

optionExplanations.A: A /24 contains 256 IPv4 addresses.
optionExplanations.B: The remaining capacity is reduced by reserved platform addresses.
optionExplanations.C: Terraform does not reserve the whole subnet.
optionExplanations.D: Tags are not IP endpoints.

questions.stem: Before applying the fifth-subnet exercise, what should be reviewed?

options.A: Only the presence of the new subnet name.
options.B: The password rotation setting.
options.C: Containment, overlap, and the proposed subnet-only change.

optionExplanations.A: A name alone does not prove range containment or nonoverlap.
optionExplanations.B: No password resource is declared.
optionExplanations.C: Review ensures the address plan and scope match intent.
optionExplanations.D: Metadata does not validate the new subnet range.

questions.stem: Two subnets in the same VNet are both named web-snet. What is the design issue?

options.A: Azure resolves them by tag automatically.
options.B: Only their regions distinguish them.
options.C: Terraform randomly chooses one name.
options.D: Subnet names identify distinct children and must be unique within that VNet.

optionExplanations.A: Tags do not distinguish identical child names.
optionExplanations.B: They belong to the same regional VNet.
optionExplanations.C: Names are explicitly supplied.
optionExplanations.D: Use separate names for separate child resources.

questions.stem: A repeat plan reports no changes after live prefix verification. What does that indicate?

options.A: The evaluated managed network matches the current configuration.
options.B: The network is now globally secure.
options.C: Every future peering is valid.

optionExplanations.A: It supports convergence at the time checked.
optionExplanations.B: No security policy is declared here.
optionExplanations.C: Future address plans still need review.
optionExplanations.D: No compute is in this lesson.

questions.stem: A learner claims the data tier is inaccessible because it is a separate subnet. What is the correct response?

options.A: Agree because the name data blocks packets.
options.B: Evaluate actual routing and security policies.
options.C: Assume every subnet is Internet-facing.

optionExplanations.A: Names do not filter traffic.
optionExplanations.B: Separate subnets alone are not isolation rules.
optionExplanations.C: No public endpoint is declared.
optionExplanations.D: Review the intended policy instead.

questions.stem: Why is CLZ-170's relative cost low?

options.A: Every network-connected service is free.
options.B: The Lab tag waives charges.
options.C: VNets and subnets have no direct hourly resource charge.

optionExplanations.A: Later services can be billable.
optionExplanations.B: Metadata does not change billing.
optionExplanations.C: Later gateways, peering, and traffic can add charges.
optionExplanations.D: Terraform is not a billing refund mechanism.

questions.stem: The validation script assigns terraform output -raw vnet_name to $vnet. Why use that result?

options.A: It obtains a secret administrator password.
options.B: It changes the network's name.
options.C: It grants read permission.
options.D: It reads the deployment's configured VNet name.

optionExplanations.A: The output is a network name.
optionExplanations.B: Output is a read.
optionExplanations.C: RBAC authorization remains separate.
optionExplanations.D: This avoids guessing a derived name in the CLI query.

questions.stem: Why choose a nonoverlapping production range before workloads depend on the VNet?

options.A: Later changes can disrupt connected resources and routes.
options.B: Terraform forbids every future variable change.
options.C: The website cannot show another range.

optionExplanations.A: Early planning reduces migration complexity.
optionExplanations.B: It allows changes, but consequences need review.
optionExplanations.C: Documentation can display other values.
optionExplanations.D: Private ranges can be reused elsewhere and overlap.

questions.stem: Which combination is intentionally absent from this address-planning lesson?

options.A: Resource group and VNet.
options.B: NSG, route table, VM, and public IP.
options.C: Web and application subnets.

optionExplanations.A: Both are declared.
optionExplanations.B: The lesson isolates the network address model.
optionExplanations.C: Both are declared.
optionExplanations.D: Both are declared.

questions.stem: Does mgmt-snet provide a Bastion session by itself?

options.A: Yes; all management subnets are Bastion hosts.
options.B: Only if local.tags includes ManagedBy.
options.C: No; a management subnet name does not deploy Bastion.
options.D: Yes; the /24 prefix acts as a credential.

optionExplanations.A: Naming alone does not create the host.
optionExplanations.B: That tag identifies tooling.
optionExplanations.C: Bastion is a separate service with its own requirements.
optionExplanations.D: Addresses are not authentication.

questions.stem: What should remain after successful CLZ-170 destroy and readback?

options.A: The VNet forever, because CIDRs are reserved.
options.B: A Windows VM in mgmt-snet.
options.C: A public load balancer.
options.D: No managed state addresses and no lab group in Azure.

optionExplanations.A: A deleted VNet is not a permanent owned object.
optionExplanations.B: No VM was created.
optionExplanations.C: No load balancer was created.
optionExplanations.D: The network boundary is disposable.

sources.title: Manage resource groups with Azure CLI

questions.stem: A subnet's Terraform resource references both group and VNet name. What does that describe?

options.A: Its parent network's Azure management path.
options.B: An independent subscription.
options.C: A generated administrator identity.

optionExplanations.A: A subnet is a child resource of a VNet.
optionExplanations.B: It does not create a subscription.
optionExplanations.C: No identity resource is declared.
optionExplanations.D: It is not a DNS record.

questions.stem: Which production enhancement follows the address foundation appropriately?

options.A: Assume four subnet names are complete security.
options.B: Add designed DNS, NSGs, routes, and hub connectivity.
options.C: Open all ports before planning routes.

optionExplanations.A: Labels are insufficient.
optionExplanations.B: These layers build on the reviewed IP plan.
optionExplanations.C: That disregards least exposure.
optionExplanations.D: Metadata must not store secrets.

questions.stem: After choosing compatible ranges, should the learner assume VNet peering is automatically transitive through a third VNet?

options.A: Yes; any two peers inherit all other peers.
options.B: Only if subnet names match.
options.C: No; peering relationships are not automatically transitive.
options.D: Yes; the Project tag enables global routing.

optionExplanations.A: Peering does not work that way.
optionExplanations.B: Names do not create transit.
optionExplanations.C: A hub design needs deliberate routing/connectivity.
optionExplanations.D: Tags do not establish connectivity.
